subtitulo: Walking a listener through a buying decision
descripcion: Discourse markers are the difference between speech that is understood and speech that is followed. At C1 the job isn't adding *however* to writing — it's managing a spoken turn of two or three minutes so the listener always knows where they are: what's coming, what's a digression, what's the main point returning. Spoken and written markers are largely different sets, and using written ones in speech is the commonest C1 register error.

filas: *There are two things going on here* / *Let me take those in turn*
*Granted* / *Fair enough, but…* / *True up to a point*
*Or to put it another way* / *What I mean is*

ejemplos.texto: *There are two things going on here. Let me take those in turn.*
*Granted, the numbers moved. Then again, they moved from a very low base.*
*Just as an aside — and this isn't the main point — the timing was odd. Anyway, the upshot is that nobody checked.*
*Anyway, the upshot is that nobody checked.*

notas: *Actually* marks correction or surprise, not emphasis. *Actually, it was cheaper* implies you expected otherwise.
*Basically* is a filler; *essentially* is a marker. Not interchangeable.
*Anyway* is the standard return-from-digression signal in speech. Learners rarely use it; natives use it constantly.

es.en: Spanish «*en realidad*» maps onto *actually* only about half the time — often it's just *well*. «*De hecho*» is *in fact*. Treating them as one-to-one equivalents is where most misuse starts.
es.es: El español «en realidad» solo corresponde a «actually» aproximadamente la mitad de las veces; muchas veces es simplemente «well». «De hecho» es «in fact». Tratar estos elementos como equivalentes uno a uno es donde empieza la mayor parte del mal uso.

de.en: «Eigentlich» maps onto actually only part of the time, and German speakers tend to overuse actually. «Also» is a false friend (it means so), while «übrigens» corresponds well to by the way.
de.de: «Eigentlich» entspricht nur manchmal «actually», und Deutschsprachige verwenden «actually» deshalb oft zu häufig. «Also» ist ein falscher Freund und bedeutet «so», während «übrigens» gut «by the way» entspricht.

it.en: «In realtà» often corresponds to actually, but «infatti» is a false friend: it means indeed, not in fact. Treating these as one-to-one equivalents is where most misuse starts.
it.it: «In realtà» corrisponde spesso a «actually», ma «infatti» è un falso amico: significa «indeed», non «in fact». Trattare queste forme come equivalenti uno a uno è all'origine di molti usi scorretti.

fr.en: «En fait» corresponds well to actually, but «en effet» is a false friend: it means indeed, not in effect. Treating these as one-to-one equivalents is where most misuse starts.
fr.fr: «En fait» correspond bien à «actually», mais «en effet» est un faux ami : il signifie «indeed», pas «in effect». Traiter ces formes comme des équivalents un à un est à l'origine de nombreux emplois fautifs.

pt.en: «Na verdade» corresponds well to actually, and «de facto» to indeed or in fact; «aliás» is a false friend meaning besides or actually. Treating these as one-to-one equivalents is where most misuse starts.
pt.pt: «Na verdade» corresponde bem a «actually», e «de fato» a «indeed» ou «in fact»; «aliás» é um falso amigo que significa «besides» ou às vezes «actually». Tratar tudo como equivalência um a um é onde começa grande parte do uso incorreto.

errores: *In the other hand* — it's *on the other hand*.
*At the end* meaning *finally* — use *in the end*.
Stacking: *So, basically, at the end of the day, essentially…*

es: «*en definitiva*» rendered as *definitively* instead of *in short* or *ultimately*.
de: «*schliesslich*» rendered as *finally* in the sense 'after all': *Finally, he is the boss* instead of *After all, he is the boss*.
it: «*in definitiva*» rendered as *definitively* instead of *in short* or *ultimately*.
fr: «*en définitive*» rendered as *definitively* instead of *in short* or *ultimately*.
pt: «*aliás*» rendered as *alias* instead of *in fact* or *by the way*.

redemittel.expresion: Let me take those in turn

traducciones.de: Gehen wir die Punkte der Reihe nach durch.

traducciones.fr: Quoi qu’il en soit, le point est…
traducciones.pt: De qualquer forma, a questão é…

redemittel.expresion: Or to put it another way

traducciones.it: O, per dirla in un altro modo…

mision.consigna: Talk someone through how you decide on a big purchase, from first idea to buying.
requisitos: a spoken turn of at least two minutes
*Let me take those in turn* to announce the structure
one marked digression (*Just as an aside*) and a return
use *to shop around*, *warranty* and *a hard sell*

microtareas.texto: Write the five markers you'll use and where they go.
Say your *purchase decision* process out loud with no markers. Then with them.
Record 2 minutes on whether *haggling over the price* is acceptable where you live. End with *The upshot is*.

autochequeo: Eight different markers, or three used repeatedly?
Any written-only marker in a spoken piece?
Did I signal my structure in the first two sentences?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on discourse markers and linking. (1) List every marker I used and say whether it works in spoken register. (2) Flag any written-only markers. (3) Show me where a listener would lose the thread and which marker was missing. (4) Flag any stacking. Do not rewrite the text.
